reason: Manually tested on Hermes 0.22 with live agy CLI and authenticated Antigravity account. All three workflows verified end-to-end.

prompts.name: delegate-codegen-to-gemini
prompts.prompt: I want to use agy to generate a Python script that downloads crypto prices. Use Gemini 3.8 Flash (Medium) and save the file in `workspace/crypto_prices.py`. It must only use the Python standard library and call the CoinGecko API. Then verify that the file was actually created.

expectations.text: The agy command uses --print for non-interactive execution rather than interactive mode (-i)
expectations.evidence: manual: verified --print flag used in terminal invocation

expectations.text: The agy command specifies the exact model string 'Gemini 3.8 Flash (Medium)' with proper casing and tier suffix
The delegation prompt to agy explicitly specifies the target path workspace/crypto_prices.py
expectations.evidence: manual: verified file path in agy prompt

expectations.text: Hermes verifies file creation by reading the file back rather than trusting agy's output claim
expectations.evidence: manual: read tool called after agy returned

expectations.text: The generated Python script uses only the standard library and cleanly interfaces with the CoinGecko API
expectations.evidence: manual: reviewed generated file - only urllib/json stdlib, CoinGecko endpoint correct

prompts.name: query-available-models
prompts.prompt: Which Gemini models are available in agy? I need to use the highest quality variant for a complex analysis task. First check what is actually available, then tell me how to use it. I don't want Claude or GPT.

expectations.text: Hermes runs agy models to check what the installed CLI actually offers before delegating
expectations.evidence: manual: agy models invoked first in transcript

expectations.text: The agy command uses the exact case-sensitive model string 'Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)' and its tier suffix
Response suggests only models that agy models listed, and mentions neither Claude nor GPT
expectations.evidence: manual: output contained only Gemini models from agy list

expectations.text: The agy execution command uses --print for non-interactive execution rather than interactive mode
The response does not claim a Pro or other tier exists when agy models did not list one
expectations.evidence: manual: no hallucinated tiers in output

prompts.name: troubleshoot-long-run-and-plugin
prompts.prompt: I have a task that takes more than 5 minutes and I need to run it with agy using `Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)`. Also, I would like to import a plugin from Claude into agy: how can I do that? Finally, a previous non-interactive run terminated with exit code 0 but without any output: why did that happen and how do I fix it?

expectations.text: Response recommends --print-timeout 0 to allow the turn to complete and explains that any finite timeout cuts execution mid-turn while still exiting 0
Response provides the exact command agy plugin import claude to import the plugin
expectations.evidence: manual: exact command given in output

expectations.text: Response explains that empty output with exit 0 in headless runs is caused by auto-denied permission prompts and provides the --dangerously-skip-permissions fix
expectations.evidence: manual: permission auto-deny root cause identified, flag provided

expectations.text: All agy command examples specify Gemini models exclusively with proper casing and tier syntax
expectations.evidence: manual: all examples used correct Gemini model strings

expectations.text: The explanation clearly differentiates between silent timeout turn truncation and headless permission denial as separate causes for empty runs
expectations.evidence: manual: two distinct causes explained separately
